purpose: Glycopyrronium is used to treat chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) by helping to keep your airways open so you can breathe more easily. It is also used to reduce excessive saliva or drooling in some patients. In certain forms, it is used before surgery to dry up secretions in the mouth and throat.
how_it_works: Your airways have natural receptors that, when triggered, cause the muscles around them to tighten and produce extra mucus. Glycopyrronium blocks these receptors, which relaxes and opens up your airways so air can flow in and out more freely. Think of it like releasing a squeeze on a garden hose so water can flow through more easily.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include dry mouth, constipation, difficulty urinating, blurred vision, and a fast heartbeat. You may also experience dry eyes, headache, or an upset stomach. These effects happen because the medication reduces moisture and relaxes smooth muscles throughout the body.
warnings: Do not use this medicine if you have glaucoma (increased eye pressure), an enlarged prostate, or a blockage in your bladder or intestines, as it can make these conditions worse. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or heart problems before using this medication. Avoid getting the inhaled powder in your eyes. This medicine is not a rescue inhaler, so do not use it during a sudden breathing attack.
typical_dosing: For COPD in inhaler form, the usual dose is one capsule inhaled once daily using the Breezhaler device, at the same time each day. For the liquid form used for drooling, dosing is based on body weight and is given several times a day. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions for your situation.
